current_linked_evidence.freshness: 1.0 (EVERGREEN: an OBSERVED restatement of a publication does not decay)

current_linked_evidence.does_not_establish: readers (a request is not a reader); a trend (adjacent-day movement inside one stream, and the calendar does not cancel); demand, adoption, buyers, money, or anything about the people making the requests

dominance.rule: X dominates Y when X is at least as good as Y on every gain field, decision impact, execution cost, external dependency and overinterpretation risk, and strictly better on at least one; dominance is a VETO on the dominated candidate, never a selection rule; vetoes from section 10 are applied independently and first
dominance.selection_trade_off: M3 carries the single most decision-relevant dimension for the existing hypothesis and is the only frontier candidate other than the winner. It loses on reachability, not on value: it needs a governance decision on a product-grain source or a reviewed category relation nobody found an authority for, and then an acquisition, against a grain mismatch Mission 1.33 found architectural. M6 reaches three commercial dimensions from rows already held, reviewed and scorable, with one governance question in front of synthesis and none in front of selection. An executable move that opens a second hypothesis defeats a theoretically better move that cannot start.
dominance.frontier_note: M2 is on the frontier and vetoed: nothing dominates its dimension and semantic gains, and it depends on a parked semantic relation. Dominance and veto are applied independently; a vetoed frontier candidate cannot be selected, and the gate computed this list, not the author. M5 is dominated by M3 on every field and strictly on impact, risk and dependency, which the author had not noticed and the gate did.
